EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows both aromatic and aliphatic C–H stretches (3040–3057 and 2870–2921 cm⁻¹; GFQ-003) and a conjugated/aromatic carbonyl near 1620 cm⁻¹ consistent with an aryl ketone whose C=O is lowered by conjugation (GFQ-011). The phenolic O–H stretch appears around 3343–3427 cm⁻¹ (GFQ-001), and a strong band near 1221 cm⁻¹ matches a phenolic/aromatic C–O stretch. The 1383 cm⁻¹ band fits a CH₃ deformation in the acetyl group (within CH bending region per GFQ-003). Strong ring modes at 842 and 650 cm⁻¹ are consistent with substituted benzene ring vibrations. Candidates lacking OH (e.g., 2, 9, 10) do not explain the 3343–3427 cm⁻¹ features; sulfur-hydride (1) would require an S–H stretch near 2550–2620 cm⁻¹ (GFQ-005), which is absent. Overall, CC(=O)c1cccc(O)c1 best matches the combined aromatic, carbonyl, and phenolic features.
